**Reference:** *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), Chapter 7, §7.3. This tutorial uses independent wording, derivations and order data.

## The question we need to answer

Quadratic regression losses have a useful property: local minima are global minima. Convexity is the mathematical reason some optimisation procedures are predictable.

## Formal relationship

$$
f(\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y)\leq\alpha f(x)+(1-\alpha)f(y),\qquad 0\leq\alpha\leq1
$$

The notation makes the assumptions and dependencies explicit. Check that the variables, sets and dimensions match the running example before drawing a conclusion.

## Derive the answer from the example

The loss f(theta)=(theta-3)^2 is convex because f''(theta)=2>0. Its only stationary point theta=3 is the global minimum. In multiple dimensions, X^T X is positive semidefinite, making squared-error regression convex.

## Interpretation and limitations

Convex does not automatically mean strictly convex: if X has dependent columns, several coefficient vectors may achieve the same minimum. Nonconvex neural networks do not inherit a global-optimum promise.

## Explain it yourself

Is -theta² convex or concave? Use its second derivative to justify the answer.
